# Muna — repository instructions for Copilot

Muna is a Windows 10/11 desktop app that recreates the macOS "notch / Dynamic Island" utility
(MacNotch parity) with Apple-grade motion and a tray-utility footprint. Read
`docs/README.md` first; it indexes every spec. **Docs are the source of truth** — if code and
docs disagree, fix one and say which.

## Stack (ADR-0001)

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri` — Rust (Tauri v2). All Windows API access lives here
  (`windows` crate). Async with `tokio`. Errors via `thiserror` + `anyhow` at edges. Logging
  via `tracing`.
- `apps/desktop/src` — React 19 + TypeScript (strict) + Tailwind v4 + Motion (framer-motion).
  State: Zustand; remote data: TanStack Query; IPC bindings generated by tauri-specta into
  `packages/contracts` — never hand-write `invoke('…')` strings.
- `packages/ui` — design system (tokens, primitives on React Aria Components, motion presets,
  icons). Every visual component has a Storybook story.
- Package manager: **pnpm**. Node 22 LTS. Rust stable (MSVC). Run commands from the repo root.

## Non-negotiables

1. **Motion & polish first.** Follow `docs/05-design-system.md` and `docs/06-motion-spec.md`
   exactly: spring presets, tokens, continuous corners, black-glass material. No ad-hoc
   durations/easings; import presets from `@muna/ui/motion`.
2. **Everything is a module** (ADR-0004). New features go in `src-tauri/src/modules/<id>` +
   `src/modules/<id>` and register in both registries; no cross-module imports.
3. **Performance budgets are requirements** (PRD §Performance): idle ≤ 0.3 % CPU, ≤ 120 MB RSS,
   ≥ 58 fps morphs. Timers/RAF/capture loops must stop when not visible.
4. **UI never touches the OS.** Platform code is Rust; the UI consumes typed events/commands.
5. **Local-first & private.** No network calls without an explicit user-enabled integration;
   secrets only in Windows Credential Manager; never log tokens or notification bodies.
6. **Accessibility**: React Aria primitives; every icon button has `aria-label`; respect
   `prefers-reduced-motion` through `MotionConfig`.
7. **UX copy**: sentence case, no exclamation marks, no jargon; empty states say what to do.

## Conventions

- TypeScript: `strict`, no `any`, no default exports except module entry `index.ts`.
  Components are function components with explicit prop types. File names `kebab-case.tsx`.
- Rust: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `unsafe` only inside `platform/`
  with a `// SAFETY:` comment; every Win32 call checks its result.
- Tests: Vitest + RTL for UI (`*.test.tsx` next to the file), `cargo test` for Rust with a
  fake platform layer, Playwright for the settings window and notch state machine.
- Commits: Conventional Commits (`feat(media): …`, `fix(shell): …`, `docs: …`).
  Include the trailer `Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`
  on agent-authored commits.
- PRs: fill `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`; attach a screen recording for any visual change.

## Validation commands

```
pnpm install
pnpm -w lint            # biome + eslint + stylelint
pnpm -w typecheck
pnpm -w test            # vitest
pnpm --filter @muna/desktop tauri dev
cargo test --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
cargo clippy --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm --filter @muna/ui storybook
```

Until the scaffold exists (milestone M0), only the docs are present; validate docs with
`pnpm dlx markdownlint-cli2 "docs/**/*.md"` and check links with
`pnpm dlx markdown-link-check`.

## Custom agents

Use the agents in `.github/agents/` for their domains (architect, shell engineer, UI engineer,
motion designer, module developer, QA, release, docs, design reviewer). Kick-off prompts per
milestone are in `docs/build-plan/`.
